before.text:
1. Introduction
                                                Katz and Sarnak [KS] have introduced the idea of a family of L–functions with an
                                             associated symmetry type. The symmetry type has been shown to govern the distribution
                                             and spacing of zeros in the function field case [KS2], and there is strong numerical evidence
                                             [Ru] that it governs the behavior of zeros in more general cases. The paper [ILS] also shows
                                             clear evidence that the symmetry type governs the distribution of low–lying zeros of a wide
                                             variety of L–functions. In this paper we give evidence that the symmetry type of a family
                                             of L–functions governs the behavior of mean values of the L–functions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The three symmetry constants have distinct large-k asymptotic fingerprints, and those fingerprints supply the growth data needed to pin down their Barnes double-Gamma representations.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 7.1 records separate expansions for log g_{k,U}, log g_{k,O}, and log g_{k,Sp}, including leading k^2 log k and symmetry-dependent lower-order terms. The source then combines these expansions with known Gamma and double-Gamma asymptotics to recover the earlier expressions for g_lambda in terms of Gamma_2.
directed.conceptual_reading: Asymptotic growth is used as an identification constraint: pole data alone permits ambiguity, while the large-parameter signature selects the intended analytic continuation for each symmetry class.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Finite integer constants are bridged to meromorphic special-function formulas by matching their large-k expansions with Gamma and Barnes double-Gamma asymptotics.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The theorem concerns integer k tending to infinity and does not validate the underlying L-function moment conjectures. Exact coefficients and constants are densely extracted and require image verification.
directed.uncertainty: The role of the expansions is clear; confidence is lower for every literal lower-order coefficient.

section_entries.label: 7. Asymptotics
section_entries.mathematical_role: Derives large-k expansions for all three symmetry constants from factorial products and Euler-Maclaurin summation, closing the double-Gamma identification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Symmetry-dependent constants have explicit large-k expansions
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Gives distinct large-k expansions for unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic g_k and explains that their combination with Gamma asymptotics fixes the Barnes double-Gamma representations.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Complicated factorial-product asymptotics are reduced to a small basis of four standard sums, so Euler–Maclaurin estimates can be reused across all symmetry cases.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Product identities rewrite sums of log(j!) and log((2j)!) using sums of log j, log(2j-1), j log j, and j log(2j-1). Lemma 7.2 supplies asymptotic expansions for those four quantities, derived from Stirling and Euler–Maclaurin and including zeta-derivative constants; substituting them completes Theorem 7.1.
directed.conceptual_reading: The calculation is compressed by choosing a shared asymptotic basis. Once each factorial product is expressed in that basis, symmetry-specific results differ only in linear combination rather than proof method.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Factorial and double-factorial products bridge to additive logarithmic sums, which bridge in turn to Euler–Maclaurin expansions with controlled remainders.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a reduction and calculation interface, not an independent proof of the moment conjectures. Exact constants and remainder terms in the four extracted formulas need scan verification.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the four-sum reduction and Euler–Maclaurin method; moderate-to-high risk in exact displayed coefficients.
